other_height_rules: Critical facilities: lowest floor >= 1 ft above the 500-year flood elevation; new roads crown no more than 1 ft below BFE. Freeboard is tied to BFE 'on the FIRMS of June 18, 2013' (2004 text: FIRMS of November 3, 2004). Substantial-improvement repairs within existing footprint may be at BFE.
quote: Freeboard. New construction or substantial improvement of any residential structure (including manufactured homes) shall have the lowest finished floor, including basement, elevated no lower than one (1) foot above the base flood elevation on the FIRMS of June 18, 2013.
date_quote: Freeboard. New construction or substantial improvement of any residential structure (including manufactured homes) shall have the lowest finished floor, including basement, elevated no lower than one (1) foot above the base flood elevation on the FIRMS of November 3, 2004. ... (Ord. No. O-2004-83, § 1d, 10-11-04; Ord. No. O-2005-103, § 1, 11-14-05; Ord. No. 0-2007-30, § 2, 5-14-07)  [Appendix A editor's note: Land Development Code, Ordinance No. 0-2004-57, as adopted by the City Council on July 12, 2004]
notes: Current text (Supp. 89, 2024; ch. 9 rewritten by Ord. O-19-57, 7-8-2019; former ch. 9 from O-13-28 (2013) and O-18-78 (2018)) keeps 1 ft. Oldest Municode version available (Supp. 70, Dec 2011) already has the same 1 ft residential freeboard in the 2004 Land Development Code (effective July 12, 2004; Sec. 908 amended 10-11-2004). So 1 ft was in force by 2004 at the latest; whether a pre-2004 flood ordinance had freeboard was not found -> first_freeboard_year null, history incomplete. CONFLICT: ELI case study (eli.org rockymountnccasestudy.pdf, 2016) states 'the elevation of the first floor of the structure must be 2 feet above the base flood elevation in Rocky Mount'; the ordinance text in every version I read says 1 ft, so I record 1 ft. Floodway/non-encroachment areas prohibit residential uses.

other_height_rules: Future Conditions Flood Hazard Areas (1% future-conditions floodplain, mapped beyond FEMA AE): RFPE = future conditions flood elevation + 2 ft. AO zones: depth number + 2 ft above highest adjacent grade (5 ft above HAG if no depth). A zones w/o BFE: 5 ft above highest adjacent grade. Fill required to 2 ft above BFE / future conditions elevation for new construction.
quote: Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation: The elevation above mean sea level to which the reference level of all structures and other development located within Special Flood Hazard Areas and Future Conditions Flood Hazard Areas must be protected. In Special Flood Hazard Areas where Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus two feet of freeboard.
notes: Current value (2 ft over BFE, applies to residential 'reference level' per UDO 8.4) verified in Durham City-County UDO Sec. 8.4 and Sec. 17.3 (shared city/county UDO). Adoption year of the 2 ft freeboard NOT established: the UDO amendment table shows TC05-04 'Flood Damage Protection Standards' (city effective 5/6/2006) moved the formerly separate City and County Flood Damage Protection Ordinances into UDO Art. 8 with the May 2, 2006 FIRMs (Durham Waterways newsletter Jul/Aug 2006, durhamnc.gov ArchiveCenter Item 697), but I could not open the 2006 text or the pre-2006 ordinance to confirm freeboard then; later amendments TC07-05 (floodplain fill, 2007), TC18-03 (2018), TC19-03 (2019). web.archive.org was unreachable from this environment.

other_height_rules: SFHA without BFE: at least 2 ft above highest adjacent grade. AO: depth number + 2 ft above HAG (2 ft above HAG if no depth).
quote: Regulatory flood protection elevation means the "base flood elevation" plus the "freeboard". In "special flood hazard areas" where base flood elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus two feet freeboard.
date_quote: In 2005, the city adopted a new freeboard ordinance that required all new buildings to be elevated two feet above NFIP's Base Flood Elevation.
notes: Corroborated by Municode archived version (Supplement 1, 2009-07-13): Sec. 35-255 'Within areas where base flood elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus two feet of freeboard', with history notes '(Ord. No. 2021, Art. 1-3, 2-14-05)' i.e. adopted Feb 14, 2005. Article XVI was repealed and re-enacted by Ord. No. 2019.10.01 (Oct 14, 2019) and retitled by Ord. 2021.06.02 (June 9, 2021), keeping 2 ft. history_complete=true rests on FEMA's statement that the 2005 ordinance was a 'new freeboard ordinance' meant 'to create a freeboard above the standard'; I did not read the pre-2005 ordinance text itself.

other_height_rules: SFHA without BFE: at least 2 ft above highest adjacent grade.
quote: “Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation” means the “Base Flood Elevation In “Special Flood Hazard Areas” where Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be 24 inches above at or above the BFE in “Special Flood Hazard Areas” where no BFE has been established, this elevation shall be at least two (2) feet above the highest adjacent grade. Amended 2/18/19
date_quote: This ordinance shall become effective on the 5th day of August, 2019. ... as adopted by the County Board of County Commissioners of Robeson County, North Carolina on this, the 5th day of August, 2019. [also: 'All provisions of the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance of Robeson County enacted on November 11, 1990, as amended, which are not reenacted herein are repealed.']
notes: Only source found is the county's posted ordinance PDF, headed '(ALL PROPOSED CHENGES ARE NOTED IN RED)', page footers 'January 25, 2008' (the base 2008 ordinance). In the RFPE definition the words '24 inches above' are red/highlighted (inserted) next to the black, underlined words 'at or above' with the note 'Amended 2/18/19' (I rendered the page to check; no visible strike-through, so the markup is ambiguous but reads as replacing 'at or above the BFE' with '24 inches above the BFE'). The ordinance was adopted/effective Aug 5, 2019; the definition note says amended 2/18/19, so the 2 ft may date from Feb 2019 -- year 2019 either way. Pre-2019 = BFE (0 ft) per the 2008 base text; the 1990 original was not seen. Robeson County not on Municode search (no hits); Bladen-Columbus-Robeson HMP (2020) has no Robeson freeboard statement. Applies to unincorporated county; Lumberton has its own 2 ft rule since 2005.

other_height_rules: Future conditions flood hazard areas: future-conditions 1% elevation + 2 ft. Flood hazard soils / unstudied streams draining >=1 sq mi: contour 5 vertical ft from the outer boundary of flood hazard soils; <1 sq mi: boundary elevation + 2 ft. Drainage basin study areas: that study's BFE + 2 ft. Streets in SFHA: 2 ft freeboard above 10-yr WSE.
quote: Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation The elevation to which structures and uses within floodway fringe areas and future conditions flood hazard areas are required to be elevated or floodproofed. Within areas which have approved engineered flood studies, such as the FEMA flood insurance study and floodway fringe areas, this elevation will be the “without floodway” base flood elevation plus 2 additional vertical feet.

quote: P29 The City of Greenville will revise the development standards in the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance so that new single-family residential development (not just multi-family) must be elevated two (2) feet above base flood elevation, making the standards consistent with Pitt County standards. Completed Completed; now considered a day-to-day capability.
notes: Could not read the ordinance itself: Greenville's code (Title 9, Ch. 6 Flood Damage Prevention) is on American Legal (codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/greenvillenc/...#JD_T9Ch6), which returned 403 (Cloudflare) to both curl and WebFetch; web search budget was exhausted before I could look for council minutes. Evidence is indirect and CONFLICTING within the 2020 Neuse River Regional HMP: the action-status table says action P29 (2 ft for single-family, previously only multi-family) is 'Completed', but the capability narrative (sec. 5.3.6) says 'Greenville requires a one-foot freeboard.' The City's April 2020 Program for Public Information says HVAC must be 'properly elevated and have two feet of freeboard', consistent with 2 ft. Implied history (unverified): single-family 1 ft (?) and multi-family 2 ft before an amendment adopted sometime before 2020 (probably between the prior Pitt County HMP and 2020). Treat value as provisional; verify against amlegal Title 9 Ch. 6 history notes.

other_height_rules: SFHA without BFE: at least 2 ft above highest adjacent grade. AO: FIRM depth number + 1 ft freeboard above HAG, or at least 4 ft above HAG if no depth number.
quote: Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation means the Base Flood Elevation plus the Freeboard. In Special Flood Hazard Areas where Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus one (1) foot of freeboard. In Special Flood Hazard Areas where no BFE has been established, this elevation shall be at least two (2) feet above the highest adjacent grade.
date_quote: Printed herein is the Land Development Standards of the Town of Waynesville, which derive from an ordinance adopted April 12, 2011. Amendments to the ordinance are indicated by parenthetical history notes following amended provisions. The absence of a history note indicates that the provision remains unchanged from the original ordinance.
notes: Current text (Supp. 17 Upd. 2, June 2026; Sec. 12.3 amended by O-11-21 (2021), O-38-22, O-22-24, O-44-25) still 1 ft. The oldest Municode version that prints the LDS (Supp. 4, Feb 2013) has the identical 'BFE plus one (1) foot of freeboard' definition with no history note, i.e. unchanged from the LDS adopted/effective April 12, 2011; also unchanged in 2013-11 and 2016 versions. 1 ft was therefore in force by 2011 at the latest; the pre-2011 flood ordinance (former town code Ch. 154 / 'Code Ch. 34 Floods' pointed to an unprinted ordinance) was not found, so first_freeboard_year is null.
